active_projects.description:
IMPLEMENTATION TASK, small and deliberately conditional: state in Lean the reductions that carry completeness and decidability of the open language at ZTime and RTime back to their L-plus counterparts, so that each one lands automatically whenever its antecedent is discharged.

THE GAP. Task 854 landed VALIDITY transfer -- openValidIn_ztime_iff_tr and openValidIn_rtime_iff_tr in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Expressiveness/OpenFutureElimination.lean say that open-language validity at those classes is L-plus validity of the translation. Nothing states the consequences that matter: that decidability of L-plus validity at ZTime yields decidability of open-language validity at ZTime, and that completeness of an L-plus proof system at ZTime or RTime yields completeness for the open language there. Those steps are short given what is landed, and nobody owns them.

WHY STATE THEM WHILE THE ANTECEDENTS ARE OPEN. Both antecedents are genuinely open -- Decidable PlusValidZTime is stated nowhere in the tree, and completeness of any recursive extension of TM-plus is open at every frame class. That is precisely the argument for landing the reductions now rather than later: the reduction is the durable artifact, and making it machine-checked means the open-language result follows by application the moment the L-plus result arrives, instead of being rediscovered by whoever lands it. State each result as an explicit implication or a Decidable instance taking the L-plus fact as a hypothesis.

ROW DISCIPLINE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE RISK HERE. Every landed row must make the hypothesis the leading clause, exactly as the openValidIn_ztime_iff_tr row does. No row, docstring or README cell may read as if decidability or completeness of the open language has been established at any class. The module docstring states what is proved -- the reduction -- and names each undischarged antecedent, with the separation hypothesis that tr itself rests on named too, since these reductions inherit it.

WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE. No proof system for the open language is built here -- that is the gated L-plus-to-open-language axiomatization task, and its rationale is confined to Base and Dense where the open-future modal is genuinely stronger. Nothing is claimed at Base or Dense, where the translation does not exist. Do not attempt to discharge any antecedent. Do not touch the Independence/ modules.

GATES. Zero sorry, zero vacuous definitions; a theorem-index row per result with the conditional form stated honestly; re-measured axiom baselines pinned by scripts/check-module-invariants.sh, never typed by hand; guarded scoped build then unscoped, with check-module-invariants.sh and check-metalogic-cycles.sh green against their pre-task baselines.

active_projects.description:
IMPLEMENTATION TASK, sizeable: formalize Gabbay separation over discrete time for PlusFormula, discharging the SeparationOver hypothesis and making the open-future translation executable.

WHY NOW. This was proposed as recommendation R4 of specs/854_open_future_modal_lplus_definability/reports/01_open-future-definability-verdict.md and deliberately NOT filed there, on the stated condition that it be filed "only if a consumer needs the executable translation". Two consumers now exist. First, FormalSystem/Metalogic/Expressiveness/OpenFutureElimination.lean's two headline results, openValidIn_ztime_iff_tr and openValidIn_rtime_iff_tr, are conditional on SeparationOver -- a hypothesis standing for cited literature that this tree does not formalize -- so the unconditional verdict that the open-future modal is definable at ZTime and RTime lives only in that module's docstring with its citation, not in a pinned row. Second, any transfer of decidability through the translation needs tr to be computable, not merely to exist.

WHAT TO FORMALIZE. GHR Lemmas 10.2.1 through 10.2.8 -- the eight eliminations plus the junction-depth induction -- for PlusFormula over frames satisfying IsZTime, discharging SeparationOver TaskFrame.IsZTime. The reference is Gabbay, Hodkinson and Reynolds, Theorem 10.2.9 over the integers; Theorem 10.3.20 is the Dedekind-complete counterpart and is the natural second target, not necessarily this task's.

WHAT IS ALREADY LANDED AND MUST NOT BE REDONE. The elimination layer that CONSUMES separation is complete and compiled in OpenFutureElimination.lean: PastDet, FutDet, the syntactic bridges, OfutP and OpastP, the eliminations ofutP_or_iff and opastP_or_iff with their CNF forms ofutP_sepForm_iff and opastP_sepForm_iff, the SeparationOver predicate itself, tr, and the two validity-transfer results. This task supplies the hypothesis those results take; it does not restate them and must not weaken any of their signatures.

SIZING, AND AN HONEST WARNING. Report 01 of task 854 rates this as a sorry-free path that EXISTS and is SIZEABLE, comparable to a multi-phase implementation round. Expect the junction-depth induction to be the expensive part. Before committing, weigh it against the MSO/Rabin decidability route, which reaches a decidability answer for the open language at ZTime with no translation at all -- if that route holds, this task's value is confined to making the definability verdict unconditional and to giving an executable tr, which is real but narrower than it looks.

SCOPE. The separation development and the discharge of SeparationOver at IsZTime; the theorem-index rows that become unconditional as a result, restated from their conditional form; the re-measured axiom baselines. Do NOT touch FormalSystem/Metalogic/Independence/ -- the non-definability result at Base and Dense is a separate verdict and is unaffected, since separation does not hold there. Do not alter the metalogic-cycles allowlist.

GATES. Zero sorry, zero vacuous definitions, no new axiom beyond what the eliminations already carry. Guarded scoped build then unscoped; check-module-invariants.sh and check-metalogic-cycles.sh green against their pre-task baselines; every axiom profile measured, never hand-typed. If the development stalls, a precisely located obstruction -- which elimination resists formalization and why -- is a legitimate [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] outcome.

active_projects.description:
RESEARCH TASK, cheap and high-value: verify and record that the open-future and open-past modals are MSO-definable in the encoding that already decides L-plus validity at ZTime on paper, which would give decidability of the open language at ZTime without the Gabbay translation and without the ladder engine.

THE ARGUMENT TO CHECK. specs/559_nondeterministic_canonical_model_tm_star_completeness/reports/03_axiomatizability-rules-engine.md section 1.3 gives a five-step paper argument that L-plus ZTime validity is decidable: (1) a countable model property, closing a countable set of walks under one chosen witness walk per state and per diamond-shaped subformula; (2) pass to the cover, a countable doubly-serial oriented forest; (3) root each tree anywhere, giving a countably branching rooted tree with one unary predicate for parent-edge orientation and one per atom; (4) encode a walk with a marked time as a pair (P, x in P) where P is connected with exactly one in-neighbour and one out-neighbour at each node, and observe that truth is MSO-definable by the usual translation of Until and Since, with box-dot rendered as "for all P' containing x" and box as "for all P', for all x' in P'"; (5) read satisfiability as an MSO sentence over the full omega-branching tree and apply Rabin's theorem. If the report has moved, it is under specs/archive/.

WHAT IS NEW HERE, AND WHY IT IS CHEAP. That report never mentions the open modals -- confirm this by grep before starting, so the contribution is stated honestly. But step 4's encoding looks to accommodate them directly: the open-future modal quantifies over the possible worlds agreeing with the world of evaluation at every time up to and including the time of evaluation, which in the (P, x) encoding is a quantification over P' agreeing with P below x -- the same shape as box-dot's "for all P' containing x", with a restriction that is itself MSO-expressible. The open-past modal is the time-reflected mirror. If that is right, decidability of the open language at ZTime follows from this route with no new machinery.

WHY THIS MATTERS STRATEGICALLY. This route is INDEPENDENT of the ladder/RaySummary front: it needs neither the tpOf pumping lemma, nor the realization theorem, nor the lift to Decidable PlusValidZTime. It is also independent of the open-future elimination translation, so it needs nothing from Gabbay separation. It is therefore the cheapest available path to a decidability answer for the open language, and it should be measured before anything expensive is committed to.

GUARDRAILS. Report 03's argument is UNVERIFIED in Lean and this task does not change that -- the deliverable is a report, not a formalization, and every step must be labelled recalled/held/derived as the report format requires. Do not claim the finite model property: the report states it is not established, because folding a regular tree by subtree type forgets what lies above a node. Do not restate the ZTime decidability of the base language (without the stability modal) as if it covered this: decidableValidZTime and decidableDerivableZTime are landed for that language only and do not extend to box-dot, let alone to the open modals. State clearly which classes the argument reaches: Base, Dense and RTime are open with the obstruction located in report 03 section 1.4, and nothing here should suggest otherwise.

DELIVERABLE: a report under this task's directory, with a verdict on whether the open modals ride the MSO encoding, and -- if they do -- a recommendation on whether to file the formalization as its own task and what it would cost.

active_projects.description:
RESEARCH TASK, and the owner of a programme that is currently owned by nobody: does TM-plus extended by the limit-closure schema admit a completeness proof, and can the located obstruction to Reynolds' construction be cleared in this setting?

WHY THIS TASK EXISTS. Task 559 owned the TM-plus completeness programme and completed as a NARROWED task -- the naming-rule soundness toolkit only -- whose description states that "The LC-schema and axiomatizability discussion in report 03 is NOT part of this deliverable". The programme therefore has no owner, while docs/theorem-index.md records the two facts that make it the gating question for this whole area: the current TM-plus axiom set is incomplete at Base (plus_incomplete_base, the limit-closure formula valid on every task frame and not a Base theorem), and completeness of any recursive extension is open at every frame class and is stated nowhere in the tree.

THE CANDIDATE, AS ALREADY RECORDED. specs/559_nondeterministic_canonical_model_tm_star_completeness/reports/03_axiomatizability-rules-engine.md proposes:
  TM-plus + LC_n + LCU + the clock rule + the transposed Auxiliary-Atoms rule
and records that every ingredient has a compiled soundness core, that no frame axiom is at risk (Saturation is idle), and that the blueprint is a held paper with a full proof. Read that report before anything else; this task starts from it rather than re-deriving it. Note that the report is in a directory queued for /todo archival -- if it has moved, it is under specs/archive/.

THE LOCATED OBSTRUCTION, WHICH IS THE RESEARCH QUESTION. Reynolds' construction uses a ONE-SIDED automaton: it reads omega-words from a root. Here emergent histories are limits of splices in BOTH directions. That mismatch is the whole difficulty and it is the thing to attack. A precisely located verdict -- which step of Reynolds' construction fails, on which model shape, and whether a two-sided or doubled automaton recovers it -- is a complete outcome for this task. So is a refutation.

INGREDIENT STATUS, SO NOTHING IS RE-DERIVED. The clock rule and the plain irreflexivity rule are landed in FormalSystem/Metalogic/NamingRules.lean (clock_irr_sound, irr_sound). The Auxiliary-Atoms expansion is NOT landed and its obstruction is specific and recorded: FrameOver.ofReflectiveRegular demands Saturation, and at the forward-cone unravelled carrier none of the three routes this tree has to Saturation applies -- read NamingRules.lean lines 57-82, which states this in full. LC_n and LCU soundness are the subject of this task's dependency and will be in the library by the time this runs.

WHAT IS ALSO WORTH SETTLING HERE. Report 03 section 1.3 argues on paper that ZTime validity is decidable via an MSO encoding plus Rabin's theorem, hence recursively axiomatizable there, leaving "only a natural system" open at ZTime. Confirm or correct that reading, since it determines whether this task's question at ZTime is about existence or only about naturalness. The finite model property is NOT established and the report says why; do not assume it.

DELIVERABLE: a report under this task's directory. No library change and no completeness claim lands from this task; if a route survives scrutiny, file the implementation as its own task.

  LC_n := box-dot G-le AND_{i<n}(dstab a_i -> dstab F dstab a_{i+1}) -> dstab G-le AND_{i<n}(dstab a_i -> F dstab a_{i+1})
with indices mod n. The compiled result lcN_valid_full establishes its validity on every all-walks Z-model for every n >= 1 and arbitrary a_i. The probe imports no FormalSystem module -- it was written under a build embargo as a Mathlib-only reconstruction over a bare formula type and a raw relation W -> W -> Prop -- so every statement must be re-expressed against the repository's own TaskFrame, WorldHistory and PlusTruthAt before it will compile. The clock rule and the plain irreflexivity rule are in FormalSystem/Metalogic/NamingRules.lean (clock_irr_sound, irr_sound), landed with their four truth characterisations. NamingRules.lean is the natural sibling home for this content, but confirm the layering before committing to it.

NOT IN SCOPE. No completeness claim and no engine: this task lands soundness results and nothing more. Do not reopen the Auxiliary-Atoms expansion -- its obstruction is TaskFrame.Saturation at the unravelled carrier, located and durably recorded at NamingRules.lean lines 57-82, and it is not this task's problem. active_projects.title: Build the L^▷ proof system: OpenAxiom, OpenDerivationTree, soundness and conservativity
active_projects.description:
IMPLEMENTATION TASK, gated: build the proof system for L^▷ -- `OpenAxiom`, `OpenDerivationTree`, and their soundness recursion -- beside `FormalSystem/OpenLanguage/`'s existing semantic half, plus the two conservativity directions over TM⁺ and the collapse under `Determined`. This is a PREREQUISITE for any completeness statement about L^▷ and it is currently owed by nobody.

THE GAP THIS FILLS, VERIFIED AT FILING. `FormalSystem/OpenLanguage/` is 1,611 lines over six files (`Formula.lean`, `OpenTruth.lean`, `OpenValidity.lean`, `OpenClasses.lean`, `OpenReversal.lean`, `OpenOckhamist.lean`), sorry-free, and carries NO proof system: no axiom type, no derivation tree, no soundness theorem. Task 559 names this exact omission and the exact remedy -- "The sanctioned home for a proof system over L^▷ is a NEW OpenAxiom/OpenDerivationTree beside OpenLanguage/'s semantic half, which perturbs no existing recursion" -- and explicitly defers the work: "it is not to be built from this task either: this task reports, and files the implementation as its own lean4 task". This is that task.

DEPENDENCY, AND IT IS A HARD GATE, NOT A COURTESY. This task declares the ▷-definability check as a dependency and MUST NOT be entered before that verdict is in. If ▷ turns out L⁺-definable, L^▷ is a notational variant of L⁺, `PlusAxiom`/`PlusDerivationTree` already are its proof system, and this entire task is unnecessary -- building it first would be the single most expensive way to learn that. Re-read that verdict before planning.

WHAT TO BUILD, and the template is named rather than invented. `FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/README.md`'s "Extension recipe: adding a `PlusAxiom` constructor" is the per-constructor cost model: `PlusAxiom` is closed, exactly three declarations pattern-match on its constructors (`PlusAxiom.minFrameClass`, `plusAxiom_validIn_min`, `plusAxiom_reflect_time_validIn_min`), neither dispatch lemma has a wildcard arm, and every other module reaches the axiom type only through `minFrameClass` and the two lifted forms. Mirror that shape for `OpenAxiom`: one constructor line, one `minFrameClass` arm, one validity arm and one reflection-validity arm per schema, with the reflection arm cheap because `reflectTime` fixes ⊡ and exchanges ▷ with ◁ (`OpenReversal.lean`), so every ◁ obligation is one line from its ▷ twin through `openValid_reflectTime`.

THE SCHEMA SET, from 559's (P2) candidate, each with its soundness status as recorded there. Soundness is LARGELY PRE-BUILT and that is the reason this task is tractable: the S5 laws for ▷ and for ◁ (`ofut_k`, `of_ofut`, `ofut_four`, `ofut_five` and the four `opast` mirrors), the ordering `□ ⟹ ⊡ ⟹ ▷/◁` (`stab_of_box`, `ofut_of_stab`, `opast_of_stab`), strictness at every link, incomparability of ▷ and ◁, HN for ▷ (`hnOpen_openValid`, and refuted for ⊡ by `hnStab_refuted_sinkFrame` -- do not state HN for ⊡), and the reversal transport are all landed in `OpenLanguage/`. What is missing is the proof system, not the semantics. The two rigidity schemata `◁φ⁺ ↔ φ⁺` and `▷ψ⁻ ↔ ψ⁻` have their semantic halves landed as `PlusLanguage.truth_congr_agreeFrom` and `truth_congr_agreeUpTo`. The definability equation `⊡φ ↔ ▷◁φ` comes from the OpenLanguage landing of that biconditional -- declare that task as a dependency too, or cite its landed names if it has already run.

WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT IN SCOPE, each of these being a way to get this task wrong.
- NO COMPLETENESS CLAIM, in any form, for any frame class. This task delivers a sound system and nothing more. 559's binding obstruction is closedness of the canonical bundle and ▷/◁ supply no closure principle; `plus_incomplete_base` stands exactly as proved; `blc` stays a non-theorem; an LC_n-style schema is still required in L^▷ exactly as in L⁺. Any docstring sentence suggesting otherwise is a defect.
- ADD NO CONSTRUCTOR to `PlusFormula`, `PlusAxiom` or `PlusDerivationTree`, and do not alter `OpenFormula`'s nine constructors. The separate-inductive-plus-embedding architecture (`ofPlus : PlusFormula → OpenFormula`, constructor-to-constructor, every derived operator sharing its `PlusFormula` namesake's right-hand side so `ofPlus` commutes by `rfl`) is the pattern and it is load-bearing: mutating `PlusFormula` would turn the landed `plus_incomplete_base`, the Independence block and both conservativity directions over TM into statements about a different language, requiring re-proof rather than inheritance.
- Do NOT define ⊡ away as `▷◁`. `OpenFormula.stab` stays PRIMITIVE. The ← half of the biconditional needs `[F.IsRegular]`, so a syntactic abbreviation would change ⊡'s truth conditions off the regular class; and the decidability front's one working anchor for ⊡ is one bit per cell (`stab_mem_tpOf_iff_cell`, resting on `stab_state_only`), which routing through two non-state-local operators would lose. Definability here means a proved biconditional with the primitive retained.
- A schema valid only over a restricted frame class that no `FrameClass` tag denotes must NOT be added to the axiom type; state its validity through the frame-predicate form instead, exactly as the `PlusLanguage` recipe directs for `Determined`.

THE THREE BASELINES ANY CANDIDATE MUST MEET, from 559's own list, and they are acceptance criteria rather than suggestions. (1) Soundness over all task frames of the class, one lemma per new constructor. (2) Conservativity over TM⁺ in BOTH directions -- which the definability equation makes statable rather than conditional, in deliberate contrast to `Conservativity.starConservative_of_plusComplete`, whose hypothesis is FALSE at Base by `plus_incomplete_base`; do not model this task's conservativity statement on that one. (3) Collapse under `Determined`, where ⊡ = ▷ = ◁ = id on a deterministic frame, so the landed deterministic completeness must still be recovered.

LAYERING AND THE GATES THAT CHECK IT. Syntax-layer files import nothing from `FormalSystem/Semantics/` and no semantic module of any language -- `OpenLanguage/Formula.lean` records this as a module invariant and `scripts/check-metalogic-cycles.sh` checks the edge. Every new file under a language directory needs a row in the `LANGUAGE_FILE_LAYERS` table of `scripts/measure-refactor-partitions.py` or `check-metalogic-cycles.sh` FAILS naming the file; add the row in the same phase as the file. `docs/theorem-index.md` is the repository's single ledger and every result needs a row there: statement, fully-qualified Lean name, file, frame class, pinned axiom set. The README's generated inventory block is NOT hand-edited -- re-run `bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory`.

VERIFICATION GATE. Guarded scoped build of `FormalSystem.OpenLanguage` green, then the unscoped build for final verification; never bare `lake`. Zero `sorry`, zero vacuous definitions. `bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh` (bare form -- a flagged subset's exit 0 is not the whole gate) and `bash scripts/check-metalogic-cycles.sh` both green. Axiom sets measured per declaration and compared against the semantic halves being lifted; picking up `Classical.choice` where the semantic half was choice-free is a regression, not a new baseline.

SIZING. This is multi-dispatch work: a new axiom type, a new derivation tree, a soundness recursion over both, two conservativity directions and a collapse theorem. Expect it to be planned in phases with one schema family per phase, not landed in one round.

active_projects.title: Probe the one-sided ▷/◁ type transport against the refuted two-sided shape
active_projects.description:
RESEARCH TASK, one probe's worth of work, aimed squarely at the Stage 1 wall: does the ONE-SIDED factorization given by the open modals ▷/◁ crack the transport condition whose two-sided pointwise form is refuted? Reports and sorry-free probes under this task's directory and `specs/evidence/seam-gluing-ray-product/`; no changes to `FormalSystem/` or `Tests/`.

WHAT THIS IS, AND WHY IT IS CHEAP. The ROADMAP records it as "a conjecture recorded as one cheap probe's worth of work, not a result and not a route". RELATION TO THE OPEN CORE, so this does not duplicate it. active_projects.title: Require a plan phase to agree with its own Scope Hypothesis and to name only artifacts that exist
active_projects.description:
Close two plan-AUTHORING truthfulness gaps in `context/formats/plan-format.md`: that a phase's task list may contradict that same phase's own `**Scope Hypothesis**:` line, and that a plan may name an artifact as the thing to CORRECT without that artifact existing.

NOTHING IN EITHER REPOSITORY IS BROKEN, AND THIS IS NOT A DATA-REPAIR RECORD. Both gaps were observed during one implementation run and both were resolved inside that run -- the contradiction was resolved in favour of the task list with a rename propagated to the next phase, and the unmeetable correction task was skipped as a recorded deviation with the durable record used as the carrier instead. `plan-format.md`, `planner-agent.md`, `plan-file-scope-harvest.sh` and the originating plan are all correct as they stand; do not re-edit the originating plan and do not change any script's behaviour. This record's entire deliverable is plan-authoring prose plus its index wiring, and one investigated-and-reported decision about a mechanical check.

BOTH ITEMS ARE BATCHED INTO ONE RECORD DELIBERATELY. Each is a short prose provision in the same file, `context/formats/plan-format.md`, for the same reader (the plan author). Splitting them would create an unordered overlap on one file's prose, which the batching guardrail in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` names as a reason to batch rather than separate. They are otherwise independent and can be landed in either order.

=== ITEM 1 -- A PHASE TASK LIST THAT CONTRADICTS THAT PHASE'S OWN SCOPE HYPOTHESIS ===

MEASURED, and the costlier of the two. A plan's Phase 8 declared in its `**Scope Hypothesis**:` that two certificate predicates were deliberately NOT promoted into the library. The SAME phase's task list required promoting a theorem that is stated in terms of one of them and whose proof destructures that predicate's characterization lemma field-by-field, including the field supplied by the other. The theorem is therefore not statable, let alone provable, without promoting both. The two instructions could not both be satisfied, and the inconsistency was discovered mid-phase by the implementer rather than at authoring time.

RESOLUTION APPLIED IN-RUN, recorded so the remedy is known to work: both predicates were promoted at the shared `K`-free carrier, the statement requirement was preserved over the scope prediction, and the next phase's same-named `K`-indexed versions -- which live over a different carrier -- were renamed to carry a `K` suffix so the two layers do not collide. No pinned Challenge-block signature was affected. VERIFIED FRESH DURING THE CREATION OF THIS RECORD: the contradiction and that resolution are both still recorded in the originating plan file as an in-place deviation note on the Phase 8 task list, so the instance can be re-read if a worked example is wanted.

THE DURABLE LESSON TO RECORD, as two separately checkable conditions:

  (a) AN AUTHORING OBLIGATION. A phase's `**Scope Hypothesis**:` and that phase's task list are two assertions by the same author about the same phase. An author who writes a Scope Hypothesis naming what is deliberately EXCLUDED must check every task in that same phase against the exclusion before the phase is written. `plan-format.md`'s "Counts-are-hypotheses obligation" already makes a Scope Hypothesis a claim requiring implementation-time confirmation, and that is the right framing for a claim about the WORLD; it says nothing about a Scope Hypothesis that is inconsistent with the plan's own instructions, which no implementation-time confirmation can repair because the phase is unsatisfiable as written rather than merely mis-estimated.

  (b) THE IMPLEMENTER'S RULE FOR WHEN IT HAPPENS ANYWAY, since authoring discipline cannot close this entirely: preserve what the task list requires -- the statement, the declaration, the thing the phase exists to produce -- over the scope prediction, record the deviation in place with the reason, and propagate any consequence to later phases that named the same identifiers. Never silently drop the task to protect the prediction, and never silently widen the prediction without saying so. That is what the measured run did and it is the behaviour to sanction.

A SIBLING INSTANCE, ALREADY OWNED ELSEWHERE -- CROSS-REFERENCE IT, DO NOT CLOSE EITHER AS A DUPLICATE. The lean extension's record `lean_plan_challenge_block_authoring_contract` owns a different surface pair of this same class: a Verification criterion contradicting the plan's own pinned `## Lean Challenge Statements` block, resolved by a precedence rule (the pinned block wins, because it is immutable by design after plan time). That precedence reasoning does NOT transfer to item 1: neither a Scope Hypothesis nor a task list is pinned or immutable, so there is no immutability argument to decide which surface wins, which is exactly why item 1(b) has to be argued from what the phase exists to produce instead. State the two rules as the siblings they are, with a pointer each way, and do not restate one in the other's home.

=== ITEM 2 -- A PLAN NAMING AN ARTIFACT TO CORRECT THAT DOES NOT EXIST ===

MEASURED. The same plan's Phase 1 opened with a task reading "Correct `specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/.blocker-research.json`", and the phase's stated goal turned on retiring a stale route recommendation that this file was said to hold. When the phase ran, no such file existed in the task directory, so there was no recommendation to correct; the task was skipped as a recorded deviation and the landed route was recorded in the durable record (`specs/state.json`'s amended task description) instead.

VERIFIED FRESH DURING THE CREATION OF THIS RECORD, AND A TRAP THIS SETS. That file EXISTS NOW. It was written later in the same orchestration run by a blocker-research dispatch, after the issue was logged. DO NOT write the guidance as though that path is currently missing and do not cite its absence as a live fact -- a reader who checks will find the file present and will discount the rest of the guidance. The honest form is to state the CLASS and its remedy. This is itself the sharpest argument for the rule: the artifact's existence is a moving quantity that the plan does not control, so a plan that assumes it is wrong the moment the quantity moves, in EITHER direction.

THE CLASS IS SHARPER THAN "CONFIRM THE PATH EXISTS", AND THE GUIDANCE MUST CARRY BOTH LEVELS:

  (a) THE GENERAL RULE. When a plan names an existing artifact as the thing to CORRECT, AMEND or RETIRE -- as distinct from one the phase will CREATE -- the author must confirm at authoring time that it exists, and the task must say what the implementer does if it does not. A correction task against a path that is absent is not a task; it is a sentence that cannot be executed, and the implementer's only honest moves are to skip it or to invent a target.

  (b) THE STRONGER RULE FOR A DISPATCH-CREATED SIDECAR. The measured path is not an ordinary file: it is a machine-written orchestration sidecar whose existence is contingent on whether a particular auxiliary dispatch has run, and whose content, if it does appear, is written by that dispatch rather than by anyone the plan can consult. A plan MUST NOT make a phase's goal turn on correcting such a sidecar. The carrier for a route decision, a retirement or a withdrawn recommendation is the durable record -- the task description in `specs/state.json`, or a file under the task's own `records/` directory -- which is exactly the substitute the measured run fell back to, and which should be named in the guidance as the sanctioned carrier rather than discovered again by the next implementer.

A MECHANICAL CHECK -- INVESTIGATE IN RESEARCH AND REPORT A DECISION, DO NOT ASSUME ONE IS BUILDABLE. `plan-file-scope-harvest.sh` already harvests each phase's `Files to modify` field, so the paths a plan names are already mechanically reachable. The open question is whether a lint can soundly DISCRIMINATE a path named as a correction target (which must exist) from one named as a creation target (which must not), given that `Files to modify` is a flat list with optional free-text annotations and no field distinguishing the two. A check that flags every not-yet-existing path would fire on every legitimately new file in every plan and would be worse than no check at all. DELIVERING THE PROSE PROVISION ALONE IS AN ACCEPTABLE OUTCOME: if research finds no sound discrimination, state that finding and its reason in the completion summary and build nothing. A formal:logic task whose work is substantially Lean runs without the lean-lsp MCP path, the Lean-specific implementation contracts, and the lake build guidance that a lean4-typed task receives.

OBSERVED CASE. A completed formal:logic task ran its implement phase under general-implementation-agent across seven files, four of them requiring new Lean theorems in `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/PlusWitnessFamily/Incompleteness.lean`, a `#print axioms` baseline probe in `scripts/check-module-invariants.sh`, scoped and full `lake build` runs, and `lake build BimodalTest`. The question to answer is whether routing should become conditional on the plan's harvested `file_scope` containing `.lean` paths, and if so, where that conditional belongs: in the manifest schema (which today maps task_type to agent name with no predicate), in `command-route-agent.sh`, or in the orchestrator's dispatch composition.

(2) Decide among: leave as is and document the rationale; reroute formal:logic wholesale; or introduce a file_scope-conditional routing predicate. (3) If a conditional is chosen, specify where it lives and what it does when file_scope is absent (29 non-terminal tasks currently have no file_scope key at all, so the predicate must have a defined behavior for the unknown case, and must not silently pick the heavier agent on no evidence). Evaluate removing the TailStable junk-position obstruction at its root by carrying full labels in the sliced certificate. Research report 06_tailstable-backward-conjunct-repair.md established that undischargeable snce positions are determined by the certificate position space posAt, not by the witness family: at target bot-S-bot the closure is {bot S bot, bot} with no state shape, so posAt is the same two-label set for every certificate and LocalCoherentLab forces every label of every certifying family to be empty. Because posAt admits every coherent closure-subset agreeing with slab on state shapes only (atom/box/stab) while temporal obligations are pinned by nothing, carrying FULL labels in the certificate rather than only the state part would make posAt a singleton, so no junk position could exist for either obligation direction and arguably neither liveness filter would be needed. This was option 3 in the repair decision; the chosen repair was option 1 (mirror the filter, landing as TailStableMirror/bwdLiveAt). Option 3 was NOT rejected on the merits, only deferred, because it costs the decidable search that FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/PlusSlicedCertificate/Check.lean is built around, i.e. most of Stage 2 again. Determine whether the obstruction can be removed at the root this way, with refactoring permitted as needed to obtain the best result. The central question is whether decidability of the certificate check survives full labels, and if not, whether a weaker label refinement makes posAt small enough to drop both filters while keeping the search decidable. Compare against the landed option-1 design: with full labels, both TailStableMirror and the forward filter would become deletable and the symmetric two-filter shape in Stable.lean would collapse. Also settle whether the superset failure mode (the Fixture.cert pre-period, repaired by absorption rather than by any filter) likewise disappears under full labels or survives independently.

OPTIONAL, FILED NOT SCHEDULED -- AND LOAD-BEARING AS A CHECK. This task stays unscheduled: status HOLD (user ruling 2026-10-03; prior_status not_started), dependencies [], nothing depends on it. What has changed since it was filed is the claim that "none of the L-plus programme's recommendations rest on it." That is no longer accurate. Its 2EXPTIME lower bound -- ARGUED, not formalized -- is the sanity ceiling that three live records cite against any proposed decision procedure for L-plus. It is load-bearing as a check even while unproved.

ITS ROLE: THE SANITY CEILING. Three records USE this task's argued lower bound as the bound-sanity check -- nothing cheaper than 2EXPTIME is a credible decision procedure. All three were re-verified against the tree on 2026-10-07 (task 738), at their archive locations:

1. specs/archive/718_omega_sequence_decidability_full_lplus/reports/02_ranked-route-analysis.md (archived), the "Complexity sanity check" bullet at line 258: "the CTL* 2EXPTIME-hardness reduction (filed, argued in both directions) is the lower bound; determinization-based upper bounds are doubly exponential, which is consistent. Any proposal cheaper than 2EXPTIME is prima facie wrong. No bound committed."

2. Task 719's description (ray layer, seam gluing and stab fibre; completed and archived at specs/archive/719_ray_layer_seam_gluing_and_stab_fibre, record in specs/archive/state.json -- now provenance rather than a live document), Deliverable 5: "DO NOT LAND A COMPLEXITY CLAIM; the CTL-star 2EXPTIME lower bound is the sanity check on any proposed bound."

3. specs/archive/721_decidability_programme_review_l_and_lplus/reports/01_decidability-programme-review.md (archived) section 3.1 (L-plus routes forward), line 147 -- its Section C ruling on this task is at line 183: "the CTL* 2EXPTIME-hardness argument (task 713, ARGUED) is the lower bound on any proposed procedure; nothing cheaper is credible; no bound is committed here."

ARGUED, NOT FORMALIZED -- AND EVERY CITING RECORD MUST SAY SO. The bound is an argument in prose, not a machine-checked theorem. No Lean declaration establishes it; there is no CTL-star syntax or semantics in the tree to state it against. Every record that cites it must describe it that way, with the ARGUED qualifier attached, exactly as the three records above do. A citation that presents the bound as established, or that drops the qualifier, is a defect in that record.

NO UPPER-BOUND CLAIM MAY LAND FROM THIS TASK. The programme commits to no complexity bound. This task's content is a LOWER bound used as a ceiling: it rules proposals out, it never certifies that any procedure achieves a cost. Deriving or landing an upper-bound claim from it -- in this task's artifacts, in a citing record, or in the write-up -- is a defect, not a result. The asymmetry is the point: a lower bound says "nothing cheaper is credible", it does not say "this much suffices."

GOAL. Raise the 2EXPTIME-hardness of L-plus Z-time validity from ARGUED to MACHINE-CHECKED. The argument is given in both directions in specs/archive/706_lplus_finite_model_property_and_completeness/reports/01_lplus-finite-model-property-research.md section Q4 ("The true order of the state bound"), completing what task 703's round-2 report argued in one direction only -- now archived at specs/archive/703_lplus_compression_and_completeness/reports/02_semantics-first-compression-research.md section 1.6 ("The complexity picture").

THE REDUCTION. Translate CTL-star by A |-> stab and X |-> bottom U ., with non-strict U rendered as e or (g and (g U e)). FORWARD: a rooted total Kripke structure becomes bi-serial by adding one fresh state with a self-loop and an edge to the root, which leaves forward paths from the original states unchanged; stab at (sigma, t) with sigma t = w ranges over histories through w, whose futures are exactly the forward paths from w, and the translation is pure-future so its truth depends only on the future (truth_congr_agreeFrom). BACKWARD: from a Z-model of the translation at (sigma, t), the Kripke structure of the state graph forward-reachable from sigma t satisfies the CTL-star formula at sigma t, by the same two facts read backwards. CTL-star satisfiability is over arbitrary, possibly infinite structures, so no finiteness is needed anywhere.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY. Formalization would turn the ceiling from an argued check into a theorem-backed one: the sharpest available limit on how good ANY certificate class can be. As task 706's Q4 and the archived 703 round-2 section 1.6 record the consequence, with the reduction a theorem no complete certificate class with singly exponential, polynomially checkable certificates could exist for full L-plus without a complexity-theoretic surprise.

CANONICAL WORDING OF THE CONSEQUENCE (quote this, verbatim, in any record that repeats it). L-plus Z-time validity -- equivalently, by negation, L-plus Z-time satisfiability -- is 2EXPTIME-hard by the CTL-star reduction. ARGUED, NOT FORMALIZED: no Lean declaration establishes it. CONSEQUENCE, stated for NON-VALIDITY: if every non-valid formula had a certificate of size singly exponential in the closure size, checkable in time polynomial in the certificate's size, then non-validity (satisfiability of the negation) would be in NEXPTIME and, equivalently, validity would be in co-NEXPTIME; hence 2EXPTIME would be contained in NEXPTIME, equivalently in co-NEXPTIME, since 2EXPTIME is closed under complement. That containment is not refuted but is widely disbelieved. The two class names are the same statement read from opposite sides of the complement: a record may name either, but must say which problem it is placing (NON-VALIDITY with NEXPTIME; VALIDITY with co-NEXPTIME). This is a LOWER bound used as a ceiling: nothing cheaper than 2EXPTIME is credible. It says nothing about any cost sufficing for L-plus and must never be restated as an upper bound. Sources: 706 Q4 (validity / co-NEXPTIME reading) and 703 round-2 section 1.6 (satisfiability / NEXPTIME reading), reconciled 2026-10-07 (task 738): the apparent divergence was one of presentation, not content.

WHAT IT COSTS. A CTL-star syntax and semantics must be added to the tree, which is substantial standalone work the programme otherwise has no need for. Task 706 rates the risk that the reduction has a gap as LOW (its R4) and records it as affecting the complexity picture only.

KEEP-OR-ABANDON IS A PHASE 0 USER RULING, NOT MADE HERE. This revision records the task's role; it does not decide the task's fate and does not schedule it. The decidability-programme review's Section C (specs/archive/721_decidability_programme_review_l_and_lplus/followup-scope-spec.md, Section C at line 220) restates the choice as the user's: keep this as a write-up note, or abandon it. RECOMMENDATION ONLY, not a decision: keep it as a write-up note, because it is load-bearing as a check even while unproved -- abandoning the record would leave the three citing documents pointing at nothing. If the ruling is to abandon, the three citing records need their sanity-check bullets re-sourced to the argument's actual homes (706's Q4 and the archived 703 round-2 section 1.6) rather than to this task.

Acquire and ingest the Cmiel-Kuhlmann-Kuhlmann ball-space paper into the literature corpus, which currently has no copy of it.

Measured gap (verify rather than trust): the manuscript's def:frame carries a footnote citing \cite{Cmiel2021} for the claim that the nonempty fibers and segments form a BALL SPACE, and that Saturation is the downward-directed-intersection condition S_1^d of that hierarchy -- the nest condition S_1 with a directed system of balls in place of a nest. That citation has no local backing document: no entry matching Kuhlmann, ball space, spherically complete or ultrametric appears in ~/Projects/Literature/index.json or in specs/literature-index.json, and a filename search across ~/Projects/Literature/ returns nothing.

Why this matters rather than being bookkeeping. Research on the S1-versus-directedness question had to proceed without the primary source and was able to settle only part of it: S_1 provably suffices for the step lemma over every history with a countable domain (covering Z-time and Q-time), while directedness can only be forced over a non-archimedean duration type with an omega_1-coinitial positive cone. The converse direction S_1 -> S_1^d remains open, and the manuscript has already withdrawn its earlier "strictly stronger" wording in favour of "at least as strong as", so the strictness question is live rather than settled. Both the open direction and the ball-space framing route through the cited hierarchy, and neither can be grounded against the source while the source is absent. Note also that Mathlib has no spherical-completeness API at all, so there is no secondary formal reference to fall back on.

Scope: locate the paper (Cmiel, Kuhlmann and Kuhlmann, ball spaces; the manuscript's own bibliography entry is the starting point for exact title and venue), then run /literature to convert and index it so it is discoverable by future --lit dispatches. Record in the sub-index what the hierarchy's S_1 and S_1^d conditions are as the source states them, so later work can check the project's usage against the source's own definitions rather than against paraphrase.

Out of scope: any Lean change, and any edit to the manuscript.

Add time addition operator (+) to the bimodal logic TM. φ + ψ is true at (τ, x) iff ∃ y,z with x = y+z, φ true at (τ,y), ψ true at (τ,z). This internalizes the AddCommGroup structure of D into the object language, extending expressive power from FO[<] to FO[<,+] (Presburger arithmetic). Related to arrow logic (Venema), relevant logic (Routley-Meyer ternary frames), and separation logic (BI). Phase 1: add tadd/tsub constructors to Formula, truth clause in semantics. Phase 2: basic axioms (associativity, commutativity, identity, inverse). Phase 3: soundness proofs. Phase 4: interaction with G/H/U/S/□. Completeness (ternary canonical model) and decidability are open research problems — defer to later phases.

Add topological open set (interior) operator for dense and continuous temporal frames. On discrete ℤ the interior is trivial (discrete topology), but on dense ℚ and continuous ℝ it captures neighborhood-stable truth: Int(φ) true at t iff φ holds in an open neighborhood of t. Related to Dynamic Topological Logic (Kremer-Mints 2005), McKinsey-Tarski topological semantics for S4, and Fernandez-Duque intuitionistic temporal logic. Phase 1: add TopologicalSpace instance to TaskFrame for dense/continuous cases. Phase 2: add interior constructor to Formula with truth clause. Phase 3: axioms (S4-like: Int(φ)→φ, Int(φ)→Int(Int(φ))). Phase 4: interaction with temporal operators and S5 □. Note: DTL is not finitely axiomatizable (Fernandez-Duque 2014) — completeness may require non-standard techniques.

So the formula the scope spec writes as `□(p ∨ Fp ∨ Pp) ∧ □(p → ¬Pp)` is `phiPos`, with the disjunction right-associated as `pForm.or (fP.or pP)`. `phiPos` is the sole member of `gammaPos`; `delPos = []`, so `posFamily` refutes no `σ` and instead exhibits a model of `gammaPos`.

The oracle is stronger than a mere certificate run, and this is worth knowing before building the fixture: `WitnessFamilyExamples.phiPos_satisfiable` is a landed theorem (axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`) producing a `FrameClass.ZTime.Sat` frame, model, history and duration at which every member of `gammaPos` is true -- assembled from `posFamily.joint_countermodel` and the four `by decide` facts `posFamily_localCoherent`, `posFamily_fulfilling`, `posFamily_boxFaithful`, `posFamily_target`. Hence `phiPos.neg` is NOT ZTime-valid, as a theorem and not as a computation.

THE CROSS-CHECK: run both routes on `phiPos.neg`.
  - `Compression.decidableValidZTime phiPos.neg` must decide NEGATIVELY (it is refuting a formula
    whose negation has a proved ZTime model).
  - `decide phiPos.neg searchDepth tableauFuel fc` (signature verified: `decide (φ : Formula) (searchDepth : Nat := 10) (tableauFuel : Nat := 1000) (fc : FrameClass := .Base)`)
    must NOT report `.valid` at `fc = .ZTime`. `.fuelExhausted` is an acceptable outcome;

    broken, not merely incomplete.
  - `isValid phiPos.neg .ZTime` must not be `true`, for the same reason.
This is a cheap consistency witness the two routes have never been given, it needs none of O4, and it can be landed as a test fixture before (a) or (b). Doing it first is recommended: it either buys confidence in the engine at no cost or finds a soundness defect while the spine is still open.

On the pre-existing graph this paper was ingested in wave 1 and not opened until wave 4, by which point three tasks would have committed to designs it should have informed.

active_projects.description:
OPEN RESEARCH QUESTION, not an implementation task. Is the logic of C3 -- the domain-restricted consequence relation -- equal to Burgess-Xu without the unboundedness assumption, plus S5?

WHAT IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED (`specs/553_decide_convex_history_layer_collapse/reports/01_convex-correlate-and-consequence.md` section 4.2) is the CONTAINMENT: C3 includes classical propositional logic, S5 for box, the whole Burgess-Xu monotonicity, enrichment, accumulation, absorption and linearity block, and `modal_future`; and C3 excludes seriality and the uniformity layer. The study explicitly DECLINES the completeness claim. Establishing or refuting it is this task, and the honest starting position is that it is open.

THE FIRST OBSTACLE, which any canonical-model construction will hit immediately (`specs/553_decide_convex_history_layer_collapse/reports/01_convex-correlate-and-consequence.md` section 4.3): the germ constraint. Every C3-validity holds at every one-point germ, and `box (phi U psi)` and `box (phi S psi)` are C3-UNSATISFIABLE for every `phi` and `psi`. That is stronger than the loss of seriality: it constrains what any axiomatization of C3 could look like, since no boxed binary-tense formula can ever be a theorem. A canonical model for C3 must either accommodate germs in the box range or the box range must be cut back first.

SEQUENCING. Do not start before the box-range design choice recorded in the C3/C4 library task is settled by the author. If the box range is cut back, this task is about a DIFFERENT logic and this description must be revised before any work begins.

LITERATURE. Burgess 1982 and Xu 1988 axiomatize `U`/`S` over an arbitrary linear order BEFORE unboundedness is added, which is exactly the setting C3 lives in. Check the Literature/ index for both before starting; acquire them if absent.

Land the three agent-system context extensions recorded by the cslib omega-automata survey

active_projects.title: conclusion stage drops null-resolution issue-log entries
active_projects.description:
Close the contract gap that makes null-resolution issue-log entries invisible to the conclusion stage

THE CONCLUSION STAGE SILENTLY DROPS NULL-RESOLUTION ISSUE-LOG ENTRIES. `context/formats/issue-log.md` declares the `resolution` field optional and nullable (its field table row reads "no (nullable)", closed vocabulary `fixed_inline | worked_around | open`). `context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Filter Predicate" admits an entry into channel classification ONLY when `resolution` is `open` or `worked_around`. An entry written with `resolution: null` is therefore neither closed (`fixed_inline`, which legitimately generates no channel item) nor classified -- it reaches NO channel and is invisible to the user. Both documents are internally consistent; the gap is between them.

VERIFIED LIVE, NOT HYPOTHESIZED. `specs/749_c_bound_half_model_a_presentation_size/issues.jsonl` holds 11 entries, every one with `resolution: null` and `suggested_channel: null`. `bash .claude/scripts/orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate --session <sid> --tasks 749` returned `proposals: 0`, `wins: 4`, `unknown_classes: 6`. Of the 11 entries, 7 are `kind: "issue"` and were all dropped: six at `severity: minor` (classes `stale-citation`, `plan-deviation`, `plan-gap`, `plan-gap`, `plan-gap`, `build-failure`) and one at `severity: costly` (class `plan-deviation`). The 4 `kind: "win"` entries surfaced correctly, which confirms the aggregator is behaving exactly as written -- this is a contract mismatch, not an aggregator bug. Re-derive these counts from the live log rather than trusting them; they are a snapshot.

DECIDE AND LAND ONE OF THREE. (a) Make `resolution` REQUIRED at write time in `scripts/issue-record.sh`, so an entry cannot be recorded without one -- closes the hole at the writer, but every existing null-resolution entry across the repo stays invisible. (b) Widen the Filter Predicate to treat null-or-absent `resolution` as `open` -- the conservative reading, since an issue recorded without a resolution is an unresolved one; note this alone would have pushed 7 entries from ONE task into channel classification, so weigh proposal volume before choosing it. (c) Keep both contracts as they are and have the conclusion stage report a separate "unclassifiable (no resolution)" tally beside its unknown-class tally, so the entries are at least visible rather than dropped. Options (a) and (c) are composable; (b) subsumes neither. Whichever is chosen, the two documents MUST end up agreeing in writing -- the acceptance condition for this record is that a reader of either file can predict the other's behavior.

ALSO IN SCOPE. `suggested_channel` was null on all 7 dropped entries too. `conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Hint-Versus-Decision Rule" treats that field as a hint the orchestrator may override visibly, which presumes a hint exists; decide whether a null hint is acceptable or whether the writer should require one, and say so in the same place the `resolution` decision is recorded.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. All four file_scope paths live in a deployed, regenerated tree -- a hand edit under `.claude/**` is wiped by the next deploy and the edit will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. Implementation MUST resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring paths there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. The deployed paths are declared in file_scope only so the overlap gate can see the collision surface; they are not the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. The edited files are not under `specs/**`, so the prose must carry no task-number references and no record-versioning language; cite durable anchors (file names, section headings, field names) only.

RELATED RECORDS, FOR ORIENTATION AND NOT AS DEPENDENCY EDGES. The roadmap-generator record covering `roadmap-integration.sh`'s partial-write behavior is the sibling core-extension defect with the same source-store boundary, and the file_scope-declaration-hygiene record covers a different blindness in the same admission machinery. No dependency edge to either -- nothing here blocks on them.

=== DISPOSITION PENDING 2026-11-04 -- DO NOT DISPATCH, DO NOT ABANDON YET ===

The underlying defect is FIXED. Verified in this repository's deployed tree 2026-11-04:
context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md now states that a null or omitted `resolution` is read
identically to `open`, and `implicit_open_count` is present in both that contract and the live
output of orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate (observed returning 6 the same day). The
source-store repository's record #373 null_resolution_entries_unreachable_by_conclusion_stage,
which did that work, is `completed` with 3 artifacts.

ABANDONMENT IS RULED CORRECT BUT IS BLOCKED ON A PRECONDITION THAT CANNOT BE MET AS WRITTEN. The
migration record in that repository requires transplanting two items this record holds into the
absorbing record FIRST, and adds an explicit fail-safe: if the transplant is not possible for any
reason encountered, do NOT abandon -- report it and leave the record open. The absorbing record
#373 is CLOSED and archived, so there is no live record to amend. Checked 2026-11-04: #373 carries

This record therefore STAYS OPEN under that fail-safe. The question of where a transplant goes when
